import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sloping binary numbers: read array of binary numbers (right-justified) along diagonals of slope $-1$

*References:*
- [A105033](https://oeis.org/A105033)
-/

namespace OeisA105033

open Nat
open Finset

/-- The primary defining sequence `a`.
`a n` is defined by the formula:
$$a(n) = n - \sum_{k \ge 0, 2^{k+1} \le n, n \equiv k \pmod{2^{k+1}}} 2^{k+1}$$ -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  n - (range n).sum (fun k => if 2^(k+1) <= n ∧ n % 2^(k+1) = k then 2^(k+1) else 0)

/-- Term theorems verifying the first few values of the sequence against the official OEIS b-file -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 3 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 2 := by decide

end OeisA105033

reformulations.difference: The OEIS sum over all eligible k ≥ 0 is implemented using Finset.range n, literal remainder equality, and natural-number subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every eligible index satisfies k < 2^(k+1) ≤ n, so range n omits no summands. Since k < 2^(k+1), n % 2^(k+1) = k is equivalent to the source's congruence. The correction sum never exceeds n, so natural-number subtraction agrees with ordinary integer subtraction. These facts and the resulting equality with the source formula were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; source_value_iff also proves the corresponding equivalence for every n and proposed value m, without sorry.

sources_consulted: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A105/A105033.seq — official OEIS entry, including formulas, offset, comments, and examples
https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL8/Sloane/sloane300.tex — Applegate, Cloitre, Deléham and Sloane, Sloping Binary Numbers (2005), especially Theorem 2.2(iii)
